newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU condemns N.Korean submarine incursion to South.
newsitem.headline: EU condemns N.Korean submarine incursion to South.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday condemned the incursion of a North Korean submarine into South Korean waters last month and said Pyongyang must abide by its armistice agreements.

"The recent incursion by a North Korean submarine into South Korean waters constitutes a new and serious violation of the 1953 armistice agreement," the EU said in a statement issued by the Irish presidency.

"The EU condemns this action and urges the authorities in Pyongyang once again to cease all activities which could result in a further increase in the tension on the Korean peninsula and to abide by the terms of the armistice agreement," it said.

The submarine landed 26 North Koreans on a beach on South Korea's east coast in September. South Korean forces killed 22 of the submarine's crew and captured one, and the remaining three were believed to be still at large in the south.
South Korea said the submarine was on an infiltration mission while North Korea said it had run aground after suffering engine trouble.

The EU repeated its support for a proposal by the U.S. and South Korea to hold four-party peace talks with North Korea and China to replace the 1953 truce which ended the Korean conflict but left Seoul and Pyongyang technically still at war.
